data.text: Independent draft review: bundle.py SHA35a5ba58e9971bbcb1fe76ba0bcf0568c5e2ca09f01d26e76ee3a263e1374d1c has a witnessed overwrite race. In a disposable directory I injected another writer creating out_path immediately before os.rename, after your last lexists check. build_archive returned success and replaced those bytes. Evidence/offline-kit/publication-race-before.json retains it. Use an atomic no-clobber publication primitive (e.g. hard-link same-directory complete temp to final, then unlink temp), and a focused competing-writer regression. Avoid check-then-rename. Also guide draft needs actual fresh-directory extraction/cd steps for someone holding only ZIP, and replace checker-never-modifies-files wording with preserves input archive (create does write a new manifest). Determinism should be scoped to the runtime/compressor or use stored entries for cross-runtime stable ZIP. No need repeat house tests. Keep changes within your three files; root is read-only on them.

data.text: Two remaining acceptance points in the current repair draft: QUICKSTART says fresh unique extraction but actually uses predictable /tmp/fresh-kit, which may already contain files and unzip can overwrite/ask prompts. Use KIT=$(mktemp -d), resolve with cd/pwd -P, extract into "$KIT", cd "$KIT"; remove unrelated unused DEST until the worksheet creates its own. The five-process test is useful but does not deterministically hit the witnessed last-check/publication race (and identical payloads cannot reveal replaced bytes). Add a focused injected boundary using real files: immediately before the final link create distinct competing bytes (also a symlink destination), invoke the actual link, assert rejection preserves competitor/target and cleans own temp. Preserve the original813/814 witness; avoid broad or repeated unchanged tests.
